# Roadmap to 1.0 and beyond

## The 1.0 Gate

Väinö 1.0 is defined by a machine-checked requirements file (`docs/1.0.md`), verified by GitHub Actions on every change:

```text
Väinö 1.0 requires:

[ ] Kernel boots on x86_64
[ ] Interrupt handling works
[ ] Virtual memory works
[ ] Processes work
[ ] IPC works
[ ] Capability system works
[ ] Drivers are isolated
[ ] Local AI can generate a driver
[ ] Generated driver passes validation
[ ] UART-test passed
[ ] Hardware can be dynamically added
[ ] At least one real robotic device works
```

Until every box is proven:

```text
Väinö 1.0    🔴 NOT READY
```

A requirement is complete only with evidence — an implementation alone never checks a box. The long-term goal is automated tests behind every line, not manual claims.

## Where the project stands

Phases 0–28 built the kernel (boot, memory, processes, syscalls, IPC, userland, drivers, filesystem, hardening). Phases 29–33 built the plugin foundation (sandboxing, load/unload, IPC gateway, snapshots, distribution, self-healing). The Eeden stretch (Phases 34–37) turns the system compositional: declare a task → compose a minimal environment → run → decompose; federate capabilities across machines; generate hardware bindings at runtime; and finally pass the autonomous-lifecycle gate (boot → compose → run 30 days → decompose → core only).

See `docs/ROADMAP_EN.md` for the full phase table with files and tests.

## 1.0 is a state, not a promise

> **1.0 is not a promise. It is a state the system must prove.**

That sentence is the whole development philosophy: small measurable experiments, honest negative results, and a gate that turns green only when the machine says so.
